data.context_sentence: She ___ coffee every morning.
data.context_translation: היא ___ קפה כל בוקר.
data.grammar_hint: With he/she/it, add -s in Present Simple: "She drinks."

data.context_sentence: She ___ a great film last weekend.
data.context_translation: היא ___ סרט נהדר בסוף השבוע שעבר.
data.grammar_hint: "Last weekend" is a finished past time — use Past Simple.

data.context_sentence: I ___ to Paris three times.
data.context_translation: נסעתי לפריז שלוש פעמים.
data.grammar_hint: "Three times" as an experience uses Present Perfect.

data.context_sentence: If she ___ harder, she would pass the exam.
data.context_translation: אם היא ___ קשה יותר, היא הייתה עוברת את הבחינה.
data.grammar_hint: Second conditional: If + past simple…

data.context_sentence: The email ___ to all employees by the HR manager.
data.context_translation: האימייל ___ לכל העובדים על ידי מנהל משאבי אנוש.
data.grammar_hint: Past passive: was/were + past participle.

data.context_sentence: The professor ___ lectures I attended won a Nobel Prize.
data.context_translation: הפרופסור ___ הרצאות נכחתי בהן זכה בפרס נובל.
data.grammar_hint: "Whose" expresses possession — the professor's lectures.

data.context_sentence: She felt a deep melancholy as she looked at old family photographs.
data.context_translation: היא חשה עצבות עמוקה כשהסתכלה על תמונות ישנות של המשפחה.
data.common_mistake: Do not confuse with "sadness" — melancholy implies a reflective, lingering quality.

data.context_sentence: He was apprehensive about the job interview, barely sleeping the night before.
data.context_translation: הוא היה חרד לקראת ראיון העבודה וכמעט לא ישן בלילה שלפני.
data.common_mistake: "Apprehensive" is about anticipating something bad — not the same as generally anxious.

data.context_sentence: The crowd was exhilarated when the team scored the winning goal in extra time.
data.context_translation: הקהל היה מלא התלהבות כשהקבוצה כבשה שער הניצחון בהארכה.
data.common_mistake: Stronger than "excited" — implies a rush of energy and elation.

data.context_sentence: She felt ambivalent about moving abroad — excited for the opportunity but sad to leave her family.
data.context_translation: היא חשה בעלת רגשות מעורבים לגבי המעבר לחו"ל — נרגשת מהאפשרות אך עצובה לעזוב את משפחתה.
data.common_mistake: Does not mean "indifferent" — it means having BOTH positive and negative feelings simultaneously.

data.context_sentence: The diligent student reviewed her notes every evening without fail.
data.context_translation: הסטודנטית החרוצה עברה על הערותיה כל ערב ללא יוצא מן הכלל.
data.common_mistake: Diligent emphasises careful, persistent effort — not just being "hard-working".

data.context_sentence: The startup decided to leverage its social media following to attract new investors.
data.context_translation: הסטארט-אפ החליט למנף את כמות העוקבים שלו ברשתות החברתיות כדי למשוך משקיעים חדשים.
data.common_mistake: As a verb: "to leverage" means to use something to maximum advantage.

data.context_sentence: The new data privacy law introduced stringent requirements for all online businesses.
data.context_translation: חוק פרטיות הנתונים החדש הכניס דרישות מחמירות לכל עסקי האינטרנט.
data.common_mistake: Describes rules/conditions that are strict and difficult to satisfy.

data.context_sentence: The company implemented new safeguards to mitigate the risk of a data breach.
data.context_translation: החברה יישמה אמצעי הגנה חדשים כדי להפחית את הסיכון לפרצת נתונים.
data.common_mistake: "Mitigate" means to lessen severity — do not confuse with "eliminate".

data.context_sentence: The travel agent sent a detailed itinerary listing every hotel, flight, and excursion.
data.context_translation: סוכן הנסיעות שלח מסלול מפורט המפרט כל מלון, טיסה וטיול.
data.common_mistake: Pronounced /ɪˈtɪn.ər.ər.i/ — five syllables. Often misspelled.

data.context_sentence: They chose the scenic coastal route even though it added two hours to the drive.
data.context_translation: הם בחרו במסלול החוף הציורי למרות שהוסיף שעתיים לנסיעה.
data.common_mistake: "Scenic" relates to beautiful natural or landscape views — not decorations inside a place.

data.context_sentence: Their flight to Tokyo included a six-hour layover in Dubai.
data.context_translation: הטיסה שלהם לטוקיו כללה עצירת ביניים של שש שעות בדובאי.
data.common_mistake: In British English this is often called a "stopover". Both are correct.

data.context_sentence: The streaming platform uses an algorithm to recommend shows based on your viewing history.
data.context_translation: פלטפורמת הסטרימינג משתמשת באלגוריתם להמלצת תוכניות על בסיס היסטוריית הצפייה שלך.
data.common_mistake: Often mispronounced: /ˈæl.ɡə.rɪ.ðəm/ — stress on the first syllable.

data.context_sentence: End-to-end encryption ensures that only the sender and recipient can read the messages.
data.context_translation: הצפנה מקצה לקצה מבטיחה שרק השולח והנמען יכולים לקרוא את ההודעות.
data.common_mistake: Do not confuse "encrypt" (verb) with "encode" — encryption specifically implies security.

data.context_sentence: With the rapid pace of innovation, many skills can become obsolete within a decade.
data.context_translation: עם קצב החדשנות המהיר, מיומנויות רבות יכולות להפוך למיושנות תוך עשור.
data.common_mistake: "Obsolete" means no longer in use, not just old — something old but still used is "dated" or "vintage".

data.context_sentence: Tropical rainforests contain the greatest biodiversity of any ecosystem on Earth.
data.context_translation: יערות הגשם הטרופיים מכילים את המגוון הביולוגי הגדול ביותר מכל מערכת אקולוגית בכדור הארץ.
data.common_mistake: Refers to variety of species, not just quantity. A rainforest and a fish farm may both have many organisms but only one has true biodiversity.

data.context_sentence: The local government launched a sustainable transport initiative to reduce carbon emissions.
data.context_translation: הממשל המקומי השיק יוזמת תחבורה בת-קיימא להפחתת פליטות פחמן.
data.common_mistake: "Sustainable" means able to be maintained long-term without depleting resources — stronger than just "eco-friendly".

data.context_sentence: Before beginning the experiment, the researcher stated a clear hypothesis that she intended to test.
data.context_translation: לפני תחילת הניסוי, הציגה החוקרת השערה ברורה שבכוונתה לבדוק.
data.common_mistake: A hypothesis is a testable prediction, not yet proven. Once proven, it may become a theory.

data.context_sentence: The contract was full of ambiguity, making it hard to determine each party's responsibilities.
data.context_translation: החוזה היה מלא עמימות, מה שהקשה לקבוע את אחריות כל צד.
data.common_mistake: "Ambiguity" is a noun. The adjective is "ambiguous." The adverb is "ambiguously."

data.context_sentence: The second witness came forward to corroborate the original testimony given in court.
data.context_translation: העד השני התייצב כדי לאשר את העדות המקורית שניתנה בבית המשפט.
data.common_mistake: "Corroborate" specifically means to confirm evidence already presented — stronger than "support."

data.translation: לנשוך את הכדור — לעשות משהו כואב אך הכרחי
data.context_sentence: I hate going to the dentist, but I decided to bite the bullet and make an appointment.
data.context_translation: אני שונא ללכת לרופא שיניים, אבל החלטתי "לנשוך את הכדור" ולקבוע תור.
data.common_mistake: Do not use this idiom for physical pain alone — it specifically means accepting something unpleasant because it is necessary.

data.translation: לשרוף גשרים — לקצץ קשרים בצורה שלא ניתן לחזור
data.context_sentence: She left the company on bad terms, effectively burning bridges with most of her former colleagues.
data.context_translation: היא עזבה את החברה בתנאים רעים, ובעצם שרפה גשרים עם רוב עמיתיה לשעבר.
data.common_mistake: Usually used as a warning: "don't burn your bridges" — implying you may need those contacts later.

data.translation: על הגדר — לא להחליט לאיזה צד לעמוד
data.context_sentence: Many voters were on the fence about the new policy until the details were published.
data.context_translation: מצביעים רבים לא החליטו לגבי המדיניות החדשה עד שהפרטים פורסמו.
data.common_mistake: Means undecided between two clear options — different from "confused" (which implies lack of understanding).

data.translation: לשפוך את השעועית — לגלות סוד בטעות
data.context_sentence: He accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party when he mentioned it to her sister.
data.context_translation: הוא בטעות גילה את הסוד על מסיבת ההפתעה כשציין זאת בפני אחותה.
data.common_mistake: Always implies accidental disclosure of secret information. The "spilling" is unintentional.

data.context_sentence: The lake at dawn was completely serene, with no wind to disturb the surface.
data.context_translation: האגם בשחר היה שליו לחלוטין, ללא רוח שתפריע לפני המים.
data.common_mistake: "Serene" implies peaceful calm, often of a place or a person's expression — more poetic than just "quiet."

data.context_sentence: He tried to persuade his manager to approve the new project proposal by presenting solid data.
data.context_translation: הוא ניסה לשכנע את מנהלו לאשר את הצעת הפרויקט החדשה על ידי הצגת נתונים מוצקים.
data.common_mistake: "Persuade" requires someone to actually change their mind. "Try to persuade" does not guarantee success. Contrast with "convince."

data.context_sentence: A pragmatic leader focuses on what works in practice, not just what sounds good in theory.
data.context_translation: מנהיג פרגמטי מתמקד במה שעובד בפועל, לא רק במה שנשמע טוב בתיאוריה.
data.common_mistake: "Pragmatic" is about practical outcomes — not cold or uncaring, just realistic.

data.context_sentence: It is paradoxical that the more choices we have, the less satisfied we often feel with our decisions.
data.context_translation: זה פרדוקסלי שככל שיש לנו יותר אפשרויות, לעתים קרובות אנו מרגישים פחות מרוצים מהחלטותינו.
data.common_mistake: A paradox appears self-contradictory but may still be true — do not confuse with "ironic."

data.context_sentence: We booked our accommodation well in advance to get the best price during peak season.
data.context_translation: הזמנו את הלינה מראש כדי לקבל את המחיר הטוב ביותר בעונת השיא.
data.common_mistake: Note the spelling: double "c" and double "m". Common misspelling: "acommodation".

data.context_sentence: She felt overwhelmed by the sheer number of emails waiting in her inbox on Monday morning.
data.context_translation: היא הרגישה מוצפת מכמות האימיילים שהמתינו בתיבת הדואר שלה בבוקר יום שני.
data.common_mistake: "Overwhelmed" can be used for both negative situations (stress) and positive ones (overwhelmed with joy).

data.context_sentence: The new manager introduced a culture of accountability where every team member owned their results.
data.context_translation: המנהל החדש הכניס תרבות של אחריותיות שבה כל חבר צוות היה אחראי לתוצאותיו.
data.common_mistake: "Accountability" means being answerable for outcomes, not just being responsible for tasks.

data.context_sentence: Hello! My name is Tom.
data.context_translation: שלום! קוראים לי טום.
data.common_mistake: Use "Hello" as a general greeting. "Hi" is informal but also correct in casual settings.

data.context_sentence: Can I have a glass of water, please?
data.context_translation: אפשר לקבל כוס מים, בבקשה?
data.common_mistake: "Water" is uncountable — say "a glass of water", not "a water".

data.context_sentence: I read a book every night before bed.
data.context_translation: אני קורא ספר כל לילה לפני השינה.
data.common_mistake: "Read" is pronounced /riːd/ (present) and /red/ (past) — same spelling, different sound.

data.context_sentence: The children are happy because it is their birthday.
data.context_translation: הילדים שמחים כי זה יום ההולדת שלהם.
data.common_mistake: Use "happy" with "be": "I am happy" — not "I have happy".

data.context_sentence: She is my best friend from school.
data.context_translation: היא החברה הכי טובה שלי מבית הספר.
data.common_mistake: "Best friend" is one person. For several close friends, say "close friends".

data.context_sentence: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society, appearing in nearly every public space.
data.context_translation: סמארטפונים הפכו לנפוצים בכל מקום בחברה המודרנית, ומופיעים כמעט בכל מרחב ציבורי.
data.common_mistake: "Ubiquitous" means present everywhere — stronger than "common" or "popular".

data.context_sentence: The CEO maintained an inscrutable expression throughout the entire press conference.
data.context_translation: מנכ"ל החברה שמר על הבעה בלתי ניתנת לפענוח לאורך כל מסיבת העיתונות.
data.common_mistake: "Inscrutable" describes something impossible to read or interpret — often a face or motive.

data.context_sentence: The beauty of cherry blossoms is ephemeral, lasting only a few weeks each spring.
data.context_translation: יופי פריחת הדובדבן חולף, ונמשך רק כמה שבועות בכל אביב.
data.common_mistake: "Ephemeral" means very short-lived — not the same as "temporary" which can last months or years.

data.context_sentence: The perspicacious analyst predicted the market downturn months before it occurred.
data.context_translation: האנליסט החד-תבונה חזה את ירידת השוק חודשים לפני שהיא התרחשה.
data.common_mistake: "Perspicacious" means keenly perceptive — do not confuse with "perspicuous" (clearly expressed).

data.context_sentence: I bought a train ticket to Haifa this morning.
data.context_translation: קניתי כרטיס רכבת לחיפה הבוקר.
data.common_mistake: Say "a ticket" (countable) — not "a ticket of train".

data.context_sentence: After a long day at work, I feel very tired.
data.context_translation: אחרי יום ארוך בעבודה, אני מרגיש מאוד עייף.
data.common_mistake: Use "tired" with "be": "I am tired" — not "I have tired".

data.context_sentence: Please keep your luggage with you at all times in the airport.
data.context_translation: אנא שמרו על המזוודות שלכם איתכם בכל עת בשדה התעופה.
data.common_mistake: "Luggage" is uncountable — say "two suitcases", not "two luggages".

data.context_sentence: I am grateful for all the help you gave me during the project.
data.context_translation: אני אסיר תודה על כל העזרה שנתת לי במהלך הפרויקט.
data.common_mistake: "Grateful" is followed by "for" or "to": grateful for something, grateful to someone.

data.context_sentence: We must submit the proposal before the Friday deadline.
data.context_translation: עלינו להגיש את ההצעה לפני המועד האחרון ביום שישי.
data.common_mistake: Use "meet a deadline" or "miss a deadline" — not "finish a deadline".

data.context_sentence: You can download the app from the official website for free.
data.context_translation: אפשר להוריד את האפליקציה מהאתר הרשמי בחינם.
data.common_mistake: "Download" = receive a file. "Upload" = send a file. Do not confuse the two.

data.context_sentence: Our neighbourhood collects plastic bottles to recycle every Tuesday.
data.context_translation: השכונה שלנו אוספת בקבוקי פלסטיק למחזור בכל יום שלישי.
data.common_mistake: "Recycle" is the verb. The noun is "recycling".

data.translation: לשבור את הקרח — להתחיל שיחה בנוחות
data.context_sentence: He told a funny story to break the ice at the start of the meeting.
data.context_translation: הוא סיפר סיפור מצחיק כדי לשבור את הקרח בתחילת הפגישה.
data.common_mistake: Used for easing social tension at the start — not for literally breaking something frozen.

data.context_sentence: The researcher presented strong evidence to support her conclusion.
data.context_translation: החוקרת הציגה ראיות חזקות לתמיכה במסקנתה.
data.common_mistake: "Evidence" is usually uncountable — say "pieces of evidence", not "evidences".

data.context_sentence: They managed to negotiate a better salary after the performance review.
data.context_translation: הם הצליחו לנהל משא ומתן על משכורת טובה יותר אחרי סקירת הביצועים.
data.common_mistake: You negotiate WITH someone ABOUT something — not "negotiate someone".

data.context_sentence: We had to declare our purchases when we passed through customs.
data.context_translation: היינו צריכים להצהיר על הקניות שלנו כשעברנו במכס.
data.common_mistake: "Customs" (מכס) is always plural. Do not confuse with "costume" (תחפושת).

data.context_sentence: She felt frustrated when the software crashed again during her presentation.
data.context_translation: היא הרגישה מתוסכלת כשהתוכנה קרסה שוב במהלך המצגת שלה.
data.common_mistake: "Frustrated" describes a feeling caused by blocked progress — stronger than just "annoyed".

data.context_sentence: The video call kept freezing because our internet bandwidth was too low.
data.context_translation: שיחת הווידאו נתקעה כי רוחב הפס של האינטרנט שלנו היה נמוך מדי.
data.common_mistake: In tech, "bandwidth" can also mean mental capacity — "I don't have the bandwidth for that."

data.context_sentence: Farmers struggled after three years of severe drought in the region.
data.context_translation: חקלאים התקשו אחרי שלוש שנים של בצורת קשה באזור.
data.common_mistake: Pronounced /draʊt/ — rhymes with "out". Not "drouth".

data.context_sentence: Students were asked to analyze the poem and explain its central theme.
data.context_translation: התלמידים התבקשו לנתח את השיר ולהסביר את הנושא המרכזי שלו.
data.common_mistake: American spelling: "analyze". British spelling: "analyse". Both are correct.

data.word: Hit the nail on the head
data.translation: פגע במטרה — אמר בדיוק את הדבר הנכון
data.context_sentence: When she said the problem was poor communication, she hit the nail on the head.
data.context_translation: כשאמרה שהבעיה היא תקשורת לקויה, היא פגעה במטרה.
data.correct_answer: Hit the nail on the head
data.common_mistake: Means to describe something exactly right — not related to actual nails or hammers.

data.context_sentence: The company invited all stakeholders to review the new sustainability plan.
data.context_translation: החברה הזמינה את כל בעלי העניין לעיין בתוכנית הקיימות החדשה.
data.common_mistake: A stakeholder is anyone affected by a decision — not only shareholders.

data.context_sentence: After the long flight from New York, jet lag kept me awake until 3 a.m.
data.context_translation: אחרי הטיסה הארוכה מניו יורק, עייפות הטיסה השאירה אותי ער עד 3 בלילה.
data.common_mistake: Two words: "jet lag". You "have jet lag" or "suffer from jet lag".

data.context_sentence: Despite many setbacks, she remained resilient and rebuilt her career.
data.context_translation: למרות מכשולים רבים, היא נשארה בעלת חוסן ובנתה מחדש את הקריירה שלה.
data.common_mistake: "Resilient" means bouncing back from difficulty — not the same as "stubborn".

data.context_sentence: Scalability was the main reason investors backed the cloud platform.
data.context_translation: יכולת ההתרחבות הייתה הסיבה העיקרית שמשקיעים תמכו בפלטפורמת הענן.
data.common_mistake: In tech, scalability means handling growth without breaking — not just "size".

data.context_sentence: Deforestation in the Amazon threatens thousands of plant and animal species.
data.context_translation: בירוא היערות באמזונס מאיים על אלפי מיני צמחים ובעלי חיים.
data.common_mistake: The verb is "deforest". The opposite process is "reforestation".

data.context_sentence: Her explanation sounded plausible, but we still needed more data to confirm it.
data.context_translation: ההסבר שלה נשמע סביר, אבל עדיין היינו צריכים עוד נתונים לאישור.
data.common_mistake: "Plausible" means believable — not the same as "true" or "proven".

data.context_sentence: We live in the same city, but we only meet once in a blue moon.
data.context_translation: אנחנו גרים באותה עיר, אבל נפגשים רק לעתים רחוקות מאוד.
data.common_mistake: Means very rarely — not literally related to the colour of the moon.

data.context_sentence: The investors conducted due diligence before acquiring the startup.
data.context_translation: המשקיעים ביצעו בדיקת נאותות לפני רכישת הסטארט-אפ.
data.common_mistake: A formal business term for thorough investigation before a deal — always two words.

data.context_sentence: The small café by the harbour is the quintessential example of Mediterranean charm.
data.context_translation: הבית קפה הקטן ליד הנמל הוא הדוגמה האופיינית ביותר לקסם ים-תיכוני.
data.common_mistake: "Quintessential" means the purest, most typical example — stronger than "typical".

data.context_sentence: Thank you for helping me carry the bags.
data.context_translation: תודה שעזרת לי לסחוב את התיקים.
data.common_mistake: Say "Thank you" — not "Thanks you". "Thanks" alone is informal but correct.

data.context_sentence: Can I sit here, please?
data.context_translation: אפשר לשבת כאן, בבקשה?
data.common_mistake: "Please" goes at the end of a request in English: "Can I have water, please?"

data.context_sentence: The movie was sad, and many people cried at the end.
data.context_translation: הסרט היה עצוב, ואנשים רבים בכו בסוף.
data.common_mistake: Use "be" with adjectives: "I am sad" — not "I feel sad" only (both work, but beginners often forget "am").

data.context_sentence: The food at this restaurant is fresh and delicious.
data.context_translation: האוכל במסעדה הזו טרי וטעים.
data.common_mistake: "Food" is uncountable — say "some food" or "a meal", not "a food".

data.context_sentence: My family lives in Tel Aviv, but I study in Jerusalem.
data.context_translation: משפחתי גרה בתל אביב, אבל אני לומד בירושלים.

data.context_sentence: The children are excited about the school trip tomorrow.
data.context_translation: הילדים נרגשים מהטיול של בית הספר מחר.
data.common_mistake: "Excited about" something future. Do not confuse with "exciting" (the thing causes excitement).

data.context_sentence: We arrived at the airport two hours before our flight.
data.context_translation: הגענו לשדה התעופה שעתיים לפני הטיסה.
data.common_mistake: Use "at the airport" — not "in the airport" (unless inside a specific building).

data.context_sentence: Do not forget your passport when you travel abroad.
data.context_translation: אל תשכח את הדרכון כשאתה נוסע לחו"ל.
data.common_mistake: "Passport" is countable: "a passport" or "passports" — not "a passport card" unless it is that document.

data.context_sentence: The weather is sunny today, so let us go to the beach.
data.context_translation: מזג האוויר שמשי היום, אז בואו נלך לחוף.
data.common_mistake: "Weather" is uncountable — say "nice weather", not "a nice weather".

data.context_sentence: She felt nervous before her first presentation in English.
data.context_translation: היא הרגישה לחוצה לפני המצגת הראשונה שלה באנגלית.
data.common_mistake: "Nervous" often means anxious before an event — not the same as "angry".

data.context_sentence: We found a small restaurant that serves excellent hummus.
data.context_translation: מצאנו מסעדה קטנה שמגישה חומוס מצוין.
data.common_mistake: Pronounced /ˈres.tər.ɒnt/ or /ˈres.tə.rɑːnt/ — stress on the first syllable.

data.context_sentence: He works in an office near the city centre.
data.context_translation: הוא עובד במשרד ליד מרכז העיר.
data.common_mistake: "In the office" = at work. "At the office" also common — both are fine.

data.context_sentence: The curious student asked why the sky turns red at sunset.
data.context_translation: התלמיד הסקרן שאל למה השמיים הופכים לאדומים בשקיעה.
data.common_mistake: "Curious about" something. "Curious" describes wanting to know — not "strange" (that is "curious" as adjective for odd things).

data.context_sentence: Her parents were proud when she graduated with honours.
data.context_translation: הוריה היו גאים כשסיימה את הלימודים בהצטיינות.
data.common_mistake: "Proud of" someone or something — not "proud from".

data.context_sentence: Let us schedule a meeting for next Tuesday at ten o'clock.
data.context_translation: בואו נתזמן פגישה ליום שלישי הבא בשעה עשר.
data.common_mistake: As a verb: "schedule a meeting". As a noun: "on a tight schedule".

data.context_sentence: We made a reservation at the hotel for three nights.
data.context_translation: עשינו הזמנה במלון לשלוש לילות.
data.common_mistake: "Make a reservation" — not "do a reservation".

data.context_sentence: Choose a strong password and do not share it with anyone.
data.context_translation: בחר סיסמה חזקה ואל תשתף אותה עם אף אחד.
data.common_mistake: One word: "password". Related: "passcode" (often numeric).

data.context_sentence: Air pollution in big cities can cause serious health problems.
data.context_translation: זיהום אוויר בערים גדולות עלול לגרום לבעיות בריאות חמורות.
data.common_mistake: "Pollution" is uncountable. Say "types of pollution", not "pollutions".

data.context_sentence: She was relieved when the doctor said the test results were normal.
data.context_translation: היא הרגישה הקלה כשהרופא אמר שתוצאות הבדיקה תקינות.
data.common_mistake: "Relieved" follows something worrying that ended well — stronger than just "happy".

data.context_sentence: My colleague helped me finish the report before the deadline.
data.context_translation: עמיתי לעבודה עזר לי לסיים את הדוח לפני המועד האחרון.
data.common_mistake: "Colleague" = coworker. "Co-worker" is also correct — same meaning.

data.context_sentence: Barcelona was our final destination on a two-week tour of Spain.
data.context_translation: ברצלונה הייתה היעד הסופי שלנו בטיול של שבועיים בספרד.
data.common_mistake: "Destination" is where you are going — not where you start from.

data.context_sentence: The company updated its software to fix several security bugs.
data.context_translation: החברה עדכנה את התוכנה שלה כדי לתקן מספר באגים באבטחה.
data.common_mistake: "Software" is uncountable — say "a software program" or "applications", not "a software".

data.context_sentence: The grammar exercise was a piece of cake for her after months of practice.
data.context_translation: תרגיל הדקדוק היה קל מאוד עבורה אחרי חודשים של תרגול.
data.common_mistake: Means "very easy" — nothing to do with actual cake or food.

data.context_sentence: In conclusion, the study shows that sleep improves memory.
data.context_translation: לסיכום, המחקר מראה ששינה משפרת זיכרון.
data.common_mistake: In writing: "In conclusion" starts the final paragraph — not "To conclusion".

data.context_sentence: Listening to old songs made him feel nostalgic for his childhood summers.
data.context_translation: האזנה לשירים ישנים גרמה לו להרגיש נוסטלגיה לקיץ ילדותו.
data.common_mistake: "Nostalgic" = longing for the past. The noun is "nostalgia".

data.context_sentence: The team discussed whether the project timeline was feasible with current resources.
data.context_translation: הצוות דן האם לוח הזמנים של הפרויקט בר-ביצוע עם המשאבים הנוכחיים.
data.common_mistake: "Feasible" = can be done practically — not the same as "possible" (which is broader).

data.context_sentence: The expedition to Antarctica lasted six months and required special equipment.
data.context_translation: המשלחת לאנטארקטיקה נמשכה שישה חודשים ודרשה ציוד מיוחד.
data.common_mistake: An expedition is organised for exploration or research — more formal than "trip".

data.context_sentence: Always create a backup of important files before updating your computer.
data.context_translation: תמיד צור גיבוי של קבצים חשובים לפני עדכון המחשב.
data.common_mistake: Noun: "a backup". Verb: "back up" (two words): "Back up your data."

data.context_sentence: Many countries invest in renewable energy such as solar and wind power.
data.context_translation: מדינות רבות משקיעות באנרגיה מתחדשת כמו אנרגיה סולארית ואנרגיית רוח.
data.common_mistake: "Renewable" describes energy sources that replenish — solar, wind, hydro.

data.context_sentence: I will stay home today because I am feeling a bit under the weather.
data.context_translation: אני אשאר בבית היום כי אני מרגיש קצת לא טוב.
data.common_mistake: Mild illness only — not for serious medical conditions.

data.context_sentence: The compassionate nurse listened patiently to every patient's concerns.
data.context_translation: האחות האכפתית הקשיבה בסבלנות לדאגות של כל מטופל.
data.common_mistake: "Compassionate" shows deep care for others' suffering — stronger than "kind".

data.context_sentence: The merger created synergy by combining marketing expertise with technical skills.
data.context_translation: המיזוג יצר סינרגיה על ידי שילוב מומחיות שיווקית עם כישורים טכניים.
data.common_mistake: Business buzzword: combined effect greater than separate parts.

data.context_sentence: They spent a month backpacking through Southeast Asia on a tight budget.
data.context_translation: הם בילו חודש בטיול עם תרמיל בדרום-מזרח אסיה בתקציב מוגבל.
data.common_mistake: "Go backpacking" — travel carrying everything in a backpack, often low-cost.

data.context_sentence: Never open email attachments from unknown senders — they may contain malware.
data.context_translation: לעולם אל תפתח קבצים מצורפים מאימיילים של שולחים לא מוכרים — הם עלולים להכיל תוכנה זדונית.
data.common_mistake: Short for "malicious software" — includes viruses, ransomware, spyware.

data.context_sentence: Taking the train instead of flying reduces your carbon footprint significantly.
data.context_translation: נסיעה ברכבת במקום בטיסה מפחיתה משמעותית את טביעת הרגל הפחמנית שלך.
data.common_mistake: Measures total greenhouse gas emissions caused by a person or activity.

data.context_sentence: The professor explained the methodology used to collect and analyse the survey data.
data.context_translation: הפרופסור הסביר את המתודולוגיה ששימשה לאיסוף ולניתוח נתוני הסקר.
data.common_mistake: "Methodology" = systematic approach — broader than a single "method".

data.context_sentence: He sat in a contemplative silence, considering every option before deciding.
data.context_translation: הוא ישב בשקט מהורהר, שוקל כל אפשרות לפני ההחלטה.
data.common_mistake: "Contemplative" = deep thoughtful reflection — not the same as "confused".

data.context_sentence: Traders used arbitrage to profit from small price differences between two markets.
data.context_translation: סוחרים ניצלו פערי מחיר קטנים בין שני שווקים כדי להרוויח.
data.common_mistake: Finance term: buying low in one market and selling high in another simultaneously.

data.context_sentence: Israeli citizens can visit many European countries under a visa waiver programme.
data.context_translation: אזרחים ישראלים יכולים לבקר במדינות רבות באירופה במסגרת תוכנית פטור מוויזה.
data.common_mistake: A visa waiver lets you enter without applying for a visa — rules vary by nationality.

data.context_sentence: Blockchain technology creates a secure, decentralised record of transactions.
data.context_translation: טכנולוגיית הבלוקצ'יין יוצרת רשומה מאובטחת ומבוזרת של עסקאות.
data.common_mistake: One word. Not the same as "Bitcoin" — blockchain is the underlying technology.

data.context_sentence: The greenhouse effect traps heat in the atmosphere, warming the planet.
data.context_translation: אפקט החממה לוכד חום באטמוספירה ומחמם את כדור הארץ.
data.common_mistake: Natural process amplified by human emissions — not the same as "global warming" alone.

data.context_sentence: Losing that job turned out to be a blessing in disguise — she found a much better role.
data.context_translation: אובדן העבודה ההיא התברר כברכה במסווה — היא מצאה תפקיד הרבה יותר טוב.
data.common_mistake: Something bad that leads to something good — hindsight reveals the benefit.

data.context_sentence: The eloquent speaker moved the audience with clear, powerful language.
data.context_translation: הדובר הרהוט ריגש את הקהל בשפה ברורה ועוצמתית.
data.common_mistake: "Eloquent" = fluent and persuasive speech — not just "talkative".

data.context_sentence: The procurement department negotiated contracts with all major suppliers.
data.context_translation: מחלקת הרכש ניהלה משא ומתן על חוזים עם כל הספקים הגדולים.
data.common_mistake: Formal term for obtaining goods/services — more specific than "buying".

data.context_sentence: Her wanderlust led her to visit over thirty countries before she turned thirty.
data.context_translation: געגועיה לנסיעות הובילו אותה לבקר ביותר משלושים מדינות לפני שמלאו לה שלושים.
data.common_mistake: German-origin noun — a strong desire to travel and explore the world.

data.context_sentence: Machine learning algorithms improve as they process more training data.
data.context_translation: אלגוריתמי למידת מכונה משתפרים ככל שהם מעבדים יותר נתוני אימון.
data.common_mistake: Subset of AI — systems learn patterns from data rather than explicit rules.

data.context_sentence: Wildlife conservation efforts have helped several endangered species recover.
data.context_translation: מאמצי שימור החיות עזרו למספר מינים בסכנת הכחדה להתאושש.
data.common_mistake: "Conservation" = protecting nature. "Conversation" = talk — do not confuse spelling.

data.context_sentence: Einstein's theory caused a paradigm shift in how scientists understood physics.
data.context_translation: תורתו של איינשטיין גרמה לשינוי פרדיגמה בדרך שבה מדענים הבינו פיזיקה.
data.common_mistake: A paradigm is a framework of assumptions — "paradigm shift" = fundamental change in thinking.

data.context_sentence: She gave a wistful smile as she remembered her grandmother's kitchen.
data.context_translation: היא חייכה בגעגוע כשזכרה את המטבח של סבתה.
data.common_mistake: "Wistful" = sad longing, often for something past — gentler than "depressed".

data.context_sentence: The company announced a restructuring that would eliminate two management layers.
data.context_translation: החברה הודיעה על ארגון מחדש שיפחית שני שכבות ניהול.
data.common_mistake: Organisational change — often involves layoffs, mergers, or new departments.

data.context_sentence: They preferred villages off the beaten path to crowded tourist attractions.
data.context_translation: הם העדיפו כפרים מחוץ למסלול התיירים על פני אטרקציות תיירותיות עמוסות.
data.common_mistake: Describes remote, less-visited places — the opposite of mainstream tourism.

data.context_sentence: The neural network learned to recognise faces after training on millions of images.
data.context_translation: רשת הנוירונים למדה לזהות פנים אחרי אימון על מיליוני תמונות.
data.common_mistake: Inspired by brain structure — core technology behind many AI applications.

data.context_sentence: Scientists linked the rise in sea levels to anthropogenic climate change.
data.context_translation: מדענים קשרו את עליית מפלי הים לשינויי אקלים מקורם בפעילות אנושית.
data.common_mistake: Formal/academic: caused by human activity — opposite of "natural" causes.

data.context_sentence: Let us cut to the chase — we need a decision by Friday.
data.context_translation: בואו נעבור לעניין — אנחנו צריכים החלטה עד יום שישי.
data.common_mistake: From film editing — skip unnecessary details and get to the main point.

data.context_sentence: The meticulous editor checked every footnote and comma in the manuscript.
data.context_translation: העורך הקפדני בדק כל הערת שוליים ופסיק בכתב היד.
data.common_mistake: "Meticulous" = extreme attention to detail — stronger than "careful".

data.context_sentence: The formula is proprietary, and the company refuses to disclose its ingredients.
data.context_translation: הנוסחה קניינית, והחברה מסרבת לחשוף את הרכיבים שלה.
data.common_mistake: Owned exclusively by one company — often protected by trade secrets or patents.

data.context_sentence: His peregrination across three continents took nearly a decade to complete.
data.context_translation: מסעו הארוך בשלוש יבשות נמשך כמעט עשור.
data.common_mistake: Literary/formal word for an extended journey — rarely used in casual speech.

data.context_sentence: Quantum computing could solve certain problems far faster than classical computers.
data.context_translation: מחשוב קוונטי עלול לפתור בעיות מסוימות הרבה יותר מהר ממחשבים קלאסיים.
data.common_mistake: Uses quantum mechanics principles — still emerging, not yet mainstream.

data.context_sentence: Geologists debate whether we have entered the Anthropocene, an era shaped by human impact.
data.context_translation: גאולוגים מתווכחים האם נכנסנו לעידן האדם, עידן שמעוצב על ידי השפעה אנושית.
data.common_mistake: Proposed geological epoch — marks significant human alteration of Earth systems.

data.context_sentence: The lecture covered esoteric topics in medieval philosophy that few students understood.
data.context_translation: ההרצאה עסקה בנושאים אזוטריים בפילוסופיה של ימי הביניים שמעט תלמידים הבינו.
data.common_mistake: Known or understood by only a small group — opposite of "mainstream" or "accessible".

data.context_sentence: He was angry because someone took his seat on the bus.
data.context_translation: הוא כעס כי מישהו לקח את מקום הישיבה שלו באוטובוס.
data.common_mistake: Use "angry with/at someone" — not "angry on someone".

data.context_sentence: The little girl was scared of the dark.
data.context_translation: הילדה הקטנה פחדה מהחושך.
data.common_mistake: "Scared of" something. "Afraid of" is similar — both are common.

data.context_sentence: She felt lonely after moving to a new city.
data.context_translation: היא הרגישה בודדה אחרי שעברה לעיר חדשה.
data.common_mistake: "Lonely" = feeling alone and sad. "Alone" just means without others.

data.context_sentence: The students were bored during the long lecture.
data.context_translation: התלמידים השתעממו במהלך ההרצאה הארוכה.
data.common_mistake: "Bored" describes how you feel. "Boring" describes the thing that causes boredom.

data.context_sentence: She found a new job at a software company.
data.context_translation: היא מצאה עבודה חדשה בחברת תוכנה.
data.common_mistake: "Job" is countable: "a job". "Work" is often uncountable.

data.context_sentence: My boss asked me to finish the report by Friday.
data.context_translation: הבוס שלי ביקש ממני לסיים את הדוח עד יום שישי.
data.common_mistake: Informal but very common. Formal: "manager" or "supervisor".

data.context_sentence: Our team works well together on difficult projects.
data.context_translation: הצוות שלנו עובד היטב יחד על פרויקטים קשים.
data.common_mistake: Collective noun — "the team is" (US) or "the team are" (UK) both appear.

data.context_sentence: He negotiated a higher salary after the successful project.
data.context_translation: הוא ניהל משא ומתן על משכורת גבוהה יותר אחרי הפרויקט המוצלח.
data.common_mistake: "Salary" is usually monthly/yearly pay. "Wage" often means hourly pay.

data.context_sentence: I use my computer to write emails and study English.
data.context_translation: אני משתמש במחשב כדי לכתוב אימיילים וללמוד אנגלית.
data.common_mistake: Countable: "a computer" or "computers". Short form: "PC" (personal computer).

data.context_sentence: Please turn off your phone during the movie.
data.context_translation: אנא כבו הטלפון במהלך הסרט.
data.common_mistake: "Mobile phone" or "cell phone" in the US. Israelis often say "phone" alone.

data.context_sentence: The screen on my laptop is cracked.
data.context_translation: המסך של הלפטופ שלי שבור.
data.common_mistake: Not the same as "monitor" — a screen is any display surface.

data.context_sentence: She typed the essay quickly on her keyboard.
data.context_translation: היא הקלידה את החיבור במהירות על המקלדת.
data.common_mistake: Hardware keyboard vs on-screen keyboard on phones.

data.context_sentence: The sun is shining brightly today.
data.context_translation: השמש זורחת בבהירות היום.
data.common_mistake: Use "the sun" — we usually add "the" for this unique object.

data.context_sentence: We stayed inside because of the heavy rain.
data.context_translation: נשארנו בפנים בגלל הגשם החזק.
data.common_mistake: "Rain" is uncountable. Say "a lot of rain", not "many rains".

data.context_sentence: The children love watching animals at the zoo.
data.context_translation: הילדים אוהבים לצפות בחיות בגן החיות.
data.common_mistake: Countable: "an animal", "animals". "Wild animals" live in nature.

data.context_sentence: She watered the plant every morning.
data.context_translation: היא שפכה על הצמח כל בוקר.
data.common_mistake: As a verb, "plant" means to put seeds in soil.

data.context_sentence: The children walk to school every morning.
data.context_translation: הילדים הולכים לבית הספר כל בוקר.
data.common_mistake: "Go to school" (attend) vs "go to the school" (visit the building).

data.context_sentence: Our English teacher speaks slowly and clearly.
data.context_translation: מורת האנגלית שלנו מדברת לאט וברור.
data.common_mistake: Gender-neutral. "Professor" is for university level.

data.context_sentence: Every student must bring a notebook to class.
data.context_translation: כל תלמיד חייב להביא מחברת לשיעור.
data.common_mistake: "Pupil" is used mainly for young children in UK English.

data.context_sentence: The lesson today is about irregular verbs.
data.context_translation: השיעור היום עוסק בפעלים לא סדירים.
data.common_mistake: Countable: "a lesson". "Class" can mean the same or the group of students.

data.context_sentence: Good morning! Did you sleep well?
data.context_translation: בוקר טוב! ישנת טוב?
data.common_mistake: Use until around noon. After that: "Good afternoon" or "Good evening".

data.context_sentence: Hi Tom, how are you today?
data.context_translation: היי טום, מה שלומך היום?
data.common_mistake: Common reply: "I'm fine, thanks." Not "I'm good" in very formal settings.

data.context_sentence: Nice to meet you — I have heard a lot about your work.
data.context_translation: נעים להכיר — שמעתי הרבה על העבודה שלך.
data.common_mistake: Reply: "Nice to meet you too" or "You too."

data.context_sentence: I have to go now — see you later!
data.context_translation: אני חייב ללכת עכשיו — נתראה!
data.common_mistake: Informal farewell. Formal: "Goodbye" or "Goodbye for now."

data.context_sentence: The manager approved our request for extra budget.
data.context_translation: המנהל אישר את בקשתנו לתקציב נוסף.
data.common_mistake: More formal than "boss". "Manage" is the verb.

data.context_sentence: Please send me the weekly report by email.
data.context_translation: אנא שלח לי את הדוח השבועי באימייל.
data.common_mistake: Noun: "a report". Verb: "report a problem" to someone.

data.context_sentence: We have a team meeting every Monday at nine.
data.context_translation: יש לנו ישיבת צוות כל יום שני בשעה תשע.
data.common_mistake: "Have a meeting" — not "make a meeting" (that sounds like arranging one).

data.context_sentence: The supplier sent an invoice for the office supplies.

data.context_sentence: You can book tickets on the airline's website.

data.context_sentence: They spent the weekend hiking in nature.
data.context_translation: הם בילו את סוף השבוע בהליכה בטבע.
data.common_mistake: "In nature" = outdoors in natural settings. Uncountable.

data.context_sentence: The forest was full of birds and tall pine trees.
data.context_translation: היער היה מלא בציפורים ועצי אורן גבוהים.

data.context_sentence: The ocean waves were calm at sunrise.

data.common_mistake: "Ocean" is larger than "sea". Both can mean salt water.

data.context_sentence: Finish your homework before you watch television.
data.context_translation: סיים שיעורי הבית לפני שאתה צופה בטלוויזיה.

data.context_sentence: The final exam covers all topics from the semester.
data.context_translation: המבחן הסופי מכסה את כל הנושאים מהסמסטר.

data.context_sentence: I borrowed three books from the university library.
data.context_translation: הלוואתי שלושה ספרים מהספרייה של האוניברסיטה.
data.common_mistake: Place for books. "Librarian" is the person who works there.

data.context_sentence: The scientist spent years on research about marine life.
data.context_translation: המדען השקיע שנים במחקר על חיים ימיים.
data.common_mistake: Uncountable — "do research", not "do a research" (say "a research project").

data.context_sentence: By the way, did you remember to lock the door?
data.context_translation: אגב, זכרת לנעול הדלת?
data.common_mistake: Used to add new information. Abbreviation in chat: "BTW".

data.context_sentence: Long time no see — how have you been?
data.context_translation: כמה זמן לא נראה — מה שלומך?
data.common_mistake: Informal greeting after not seeing someone for a while.

data.context_sentence: You look stressed — take it easy and get some rest.
data.context_translation: נראה לחוץ — תירגע וקח קצת מנוחה.
data.common_mistake: Means relax / don't worry. Also used as casual goodbye.

data.context_sentence: Hang on — I need to find my keys before we leave.
data.context_translation: חכה רגע — אני צריך למצוא המפתחות לפני שאנחנו יוצאים.
data.common_mistake: Informal: wait a moment. "Hang in there" = keep going despite difficulty.

data.context_sentence: The company stores customer data in a secure database.
data.context_translation: החברה מאחסנת נתוני לקוחות במאגר נתונים מאובטח.
data.common_mistake: One word. Stores structured data — not the same as a simple "file".

data.context_sentence: Coral reefs are fragile ecosystems that support thousands of species.
data.context_translation: שוניות אלמוגים הן מערכות אקולוגיות עדינות שתומכות באלפי מינים.
data.common_mistake: Community of living things and their environment — interconnected.

data.context_sentence: Darwin's theory of evolution changed biology forever.
data.context_translation: תיאוריית האבולוציה של דארווין שינתה את הביולוגיה לנצח.
data.common_mistake: In science, a "theory" is well-supported — not just a guess.

data.word: Cost an arm and a leg
data.context_sentence: That designer bag costs an arm and a leg.
data.context_translation: התיק של המעצב עולה הון.
data.correct_answer: Cost an arm and a leg
data.common_mistake: Means very expensive — hyperbolic idiom, not literal.

data.context_sentence: We spent the afternoon sightseeing in the old city.
data.context_translation: בילינו את אחר הצהריים בסיורים בעיר העתיקה.
data.common_mistake: One word, no hyphen. "Go sightseeing" — activity of visiting attractions.

data.context_sentence: He felt anxious before the job interview.
data.context_translation: הוא הרגיש חרד לפני ראיון העבודה.
data.common_mistake: "Anxious about" the future. Similar to "nervous" but often more persistent worry.

data.context_sentence: The team stayed within budget for the marketing campaign.
data.context_translation: הצוות נשאר בתוך התקציב עבור קמפיין השיווק.
data.common_mistake: Noun and verb: "budget for" expenses. "Over budget" = spent too much.

data.context_sentence: A firewall blocks unauthorised access to the company network.
data.context_translation: חומת אש חוסמת גישה לא מורשית לרשת החברה.
data.common_mistake: Cybersecurity barrier — hardware or software.

data.context_sentence: The national park protects local wildlife and native plants.
data.context_translation: הפארק הלאומי מגן על חיות בר וצמחים מקומיים.
data.common_mistake: Uncountable — animals living in natural conditions.

data.context_sentence: Every citation in the paper must link to a reliable source.
data.context_translation: כל ציטוט במאמר חייב להפנות למקור אמין.
data.common_mistake: Academic reference to a source. "Quote" is the actual words cited.

data.context_sentence: She ___ in London for five years.
data.context_translation: היא ___ בלונדון כבר חמש שנים.
data.grammar_hint: Use Present Perfect ("has/have + past participle") for actions that started in the past and continue to the present. "For five years" signals duration up to now.
data.common_mistake: Do not use Past Simple here — "She lived in London for five years" implies she no longer does.

data.context_sentence: They ___ the project yet.
data.context_translation: הם ___ את הפרויקט עדיין.
data.grammar_hint: "Yet" is a signal word for the Present Perfect when used in negatives and questions. It means "up to now."
data.common_mistake: "Didn't finish yet" is wrong — "yet" requires Present Perfect in standard British/American English.

data.context_sentence: This is the most interesting book I ___ in years.
data.context_translation: זה הספר המעניין ביותר שאני ___ בשנים.
data.grammar_hint: After superlatives ("most interesting", "best", "worst"), use the Present Perfect to describe a personal experience.
data.common_mistake: With superlatives comparing experiences, Present Perfect is standard, not Past Simple.

data.context_sentence: She ___ her keys when she left the house.
data.context_translation: היא ___ את המפתחות שלה כשיצאה מהבית.
data.grammar_hint: Use Past Simple for a completed action at a specific moment in the past. "When she left" anchors the action to a point in time.
data.common_mistake: "When" followed by a past action usually calls for Past Simple, not Present Perfect.

data.context_sentence: Last summer, we ___ in a small cabin by the lake for two weeks.
data.context_translation: בקיץ שעבר, ___ בצריף קטן ליד האגם במשך שבועיים.
data.grammar_hint: "Last summer" is a finished time period — use Past Simple. Time phrases like "yesterday", "last year", "in 2020" always go with Past Simple.
data.common_mistake: Never use Present Perfect with a specific finished time expression like "last summer."

data.question_text: Which option correctly completes the sentence?
data.context_sentence: If I ___ more time, I would travel the world.
data.context_translation: אם היה לי יותר זמן, הייתי מטייל בעולם.
data.grammar_hint: Second Conditional (hypothetical/unreal present): "If + past simple, would + base verb." Use "had" here — it signals this is imaginary, not real.
data.common_mistake: Never use "would" in the if-clause: NOT "If I would have time."

data.context_sentence: If she ___ the warning, she would have avoided the accident.
data.context_translation: אם היא ___ את האזהרה, היא הייתה נמנעת מהתאונה.
data.grammar_hint: Third Conditional (unreal past): "If + past perfect, would have + past participle." The action cannot be changed now.
data.common_mistake: Do not mix up tenses: the if-clause needs "had + past participle", the result needs "would have + past participle."

data.context_sentence: If you ___ hard enough, you will pass the exam.
data.context_translation: אם תתאמן ___ מספיק קשה, תעבור את הבחינה.
data.grammar_hint: First Conditional (real/possible future): "If + present simple, will + base verb." The situation is possible.
data.common_mistake: Do NOT use "will" in the if-clause of first conditionals: NOT "If you will study."

data.context_sentence: The annual report ___ by the finance team last week.
data.context_translation: הדוח השנתי ___ על ידי צוות הכספים בשבוע שעבר.
data.grammar_hint: Passive voice in past simple: "was/were + past participle." The phrase "last week" confirms we need a past tense.
data.common_mistake: "Has been prepared" would mean the action was recently completed with a present-time relevance — "last week" rules this out.

data.context_sentence: A new hospital ___ in the city centre by the end of next year.
data.context_translation: בית חולים חדש ___ במרכז העיר עד סוף השנה הבאה.
data.grammar_hint: Future passive: "will be + past participle." Use for an action that will happen to the subject in the future.
data.common_mistake: "Will have been built" (future perfect passive) would be needed only if you specify a deadline by which it must be complete. Here the phrase "by the end of next year" indicates a simple planned future event.

data.question_text: Which article best fills the gap?
data.context_sentence: She is ___ honest person who always tells the truth.
data.context_translation: היא ___ אדם ישר שתמיד אומר את האמת.
data.grammar_hint: Use "an" before words beginning with a vowel SOUND. "Honest" starts with a silent "h," so it sounds like it starts with "o" — use "an."
data.common_mistake: The rule is about the SOUND, not the spelling. "A uniform" is correct because /juːnɪfɔːm/ starts with a "y" sound.

data.question_text: Choose the correct article (or no article):
data.context_sentence: ___ money does not guarantee happiness.
data.context_translation: ___ כסף אינו מבטיח אושר.
data.grammar_hint: When talking about something in general (uncountable nouns like "money", "love", "happiness"), use no article.
data.common_mistake: "The money" would refer to specific money already mentioned. No article means "money in general."

data.context_sentence: We visited ___ Eiffel Tower during our trip to Paris.
data.context_translation: ביקרנו ב ___ מגדל אייפל במהלך הטיול שלנו בפריז.
data.grammar_hint: Use "the" with unique landmarks and specific places. There is only one Eiffel Tower, so it is already specific.
data.common_mistake: "A Eiffel Tower" is wrong — use "the" for famous, unique places.

data.context_sentence: You ___ wear a helmet when cycling — it is the law.
data.context_translation: אתה ___ לחבוש קסדה בזמן רכיבה על אופניים — זה חוק.
data.grammar_hint: "Must" expresses a legal or strong external obligation. "Should" is a recommendation. When there is a law, use "must."
data.common_mistake: "Should" is advisory. "Must" is obligatory. If you break the law, "must" was the right choice.

data.question_text: Choose the best modal for this context:
data.context_sentence: She ___ be at home — her car is in the driveway.
data.context_translation: היא ___ להיות בבית — המכונית שלה בחניה.
data.grammar_hint: "Must" is also used for logical deductions based on evidence. The car in the driveway is the evidence.
data.common_mistake: "Should" implies expectation based on schedule. "Must" implies deduction from evidence — completely different meanings.

data.question_text: Which sentence expresses a past ability?
data.context_sentence: When he was young, he ___ run a marathon without stopping.
data.context_translation: כשהיה צעיר, הוא ___ לרוץ מרתון ללא עצירה.
data.grammar_hint: "Could" expresses past ability (what someone was able to do). "Would" refers to past habits. "Must have" is a past deduction.
data.common_mistake: "Would run a marathon" implies habitual action — he did it regularly. "Could run" means he had the ability (even once).

data.context_sentence: The meeting is scheduled ___ Monday at 9 a.m.
data.context_translation: הישיבה מתוכננת ___ יום שני בשעה 9 בבוקר.
data.grammar_hint: Use "on" for days of the week (on Monday), dates (on 5th March), and specific days (on New Year's Day).
data.common_mistake: "At" is for clock times, "in" is for months/years/seasons. "On" is for days.

data.context_sentence: She has been working ___ this company since 2019.
data.context_translation: היא עובדת ב ___ חברה זו מאז 2019.
data.grammar_hint: Use "for" to describe how long something has continued. Use "at" or "with" to describe where you work.
data.common_mistake: "Working at this company" is also possible, but the blank precedes "this company" here, not a time duration, so "for" fits the sentence.

data.question_text: Choose the phrasal verb that fits the context:
data.context_sentence: He could not ___ the difficult maths problem no matter how hard he tried.
data.context_translation: הוא לא הצליח ___ את בעיית המתמטיקה הקשה לא משנה כמה קשה ניסה.
data.grammar_hint: "Figure out" = to understand or solve something. "Look up" = to search for information. "Put off" = to delay. "Give in" = to surrender.
data.common_mistake: "Figure out" is separable: "figure it out" is also correct.

data.question_text: Which phrasal verb means "to cancel a plan"?
data.context_sentence: We had to ___ the outdoor concert because of the heavy rain.
data.context_translation: נאלצנו ___ את הקונצרט בחוץ בגלל הגשם הכבד.
data.grammar_hint: "Call off" means to cancel an event. "Call up" = to phone someone. "Put on" = to wear or organize.
data.common_mistake: "Cancel" and "call off" are interchangeable, but "call off" is more informal.

data.context_sentence: The new office building is ___ than the old one.
data.context_translation: בניין המשרדים החדש ___ מהישן.
data.grammar_hint: For adjectives with two or more syllables, use "more + adjective" for comparatives, not "-er".
data.common_mistake: "Moderner" is not a word. Three-syllable adjectives always use "more/most."

data.context_sentence: This is ___ meal I have ever tasted.
data.context_translation: זה ___ ארוחה שטעמתי אי פעם.
data.grammar_hint: Superlatives need "the" before them: "the most + adjective" or "the + adjective + -est". Never "the more" for superlatives.
data.common_mistake: Always include "the" before a superlative when referring to a specific instance.

data.context_sentence: The scientist ___ discovered penicillin changed medicine forever.
data.context_translation: המדען ___ גילה את הפניצילין שינה את הרפואה לנצח.
data.grammar_hint: Use "who" for people as the subject of the relative clause. Use "which" for things. Use "whose" for possession.
data.common_mistake: "Which" is for things, not people. Always use "who" or "whom" when the antecedent is a person.

data.context_sentence: The report, ___ findings were surprising, was published last month.
data.context_translation: הדו"ח, ___ ממצאיו היו מפתיעים, פורסם בחודש שעבר.
data.grammar_hint: "Whose" shows possession. The report has/owns the findings. "The report whose findings" = "the findings of the report."
data.common_mistake: "Which findings" would make it an additional clause, not possessive. "Whose" is the possessive relative pronoun for both people and things.

data.question_text: Convert to reported speech. He said: "I will finish the report tomorrow."
data.context_sentence: He said that he ___ the report the following day.
data.context_translation: הוא אמר שהוא ___ את הדו"ח למחרת.
data.grammar_hint: In reported speech, "will" shifts back to "would." Time references also shift: "tomorrow" becomes "the following day."
data.common_mistake: "Will" is direct speech. In reported speech after a past verb ("said"), always shift "will" → "would."

data.context_sentence: Right now, the engineers ___ the software for the new feature.
data.context_translation: כרגע, המהנדסים ___ את התוכנה לתכונה החדשה.
data.grammar_hint: "Right now" signals an action happening at this exact moment — use Present Continuous (am/is/are + -ing).
data.common_mistake: Present Simple ("test") describes general habits. Present Continuous describes what is happening at this moment.

data.context_sentence: I ___ English every day.
data.context_translation: אני ___ אנגלית כל יום.
data.grammar_hint: With "I/you/we/they", use the base verb in Present Simple: "I study."
data.common_mistake: "Studies" is for he/she/it. With "I", always use the base form.

data.context_sentence: She is ___ teacher.
data.context_translation: היא ___ מורה.
data.grammar_hint: Use "a" before consonant sounds and "an" before vowel sounds. "Teacher" starts with a consonant.
data.common_mistake: "An teacher" is wrong — "teacher" begins with /t/, a consonant sound.

data.context_sentence: They ___ in Tel Aviv.
data.context_translation: הם ___ בתל אביב.
data.grammar_hint: With "they/we/you/I", Present Simple uses the base verb without -s.
data.common_mistake: "Lives" is only for he/she/it: "He lives" but "They live".

data.question_text: Choose the correct third conditional form:
data.context_sentence: If the company ___ more aggressively, it would have captured the market.
data.context_translation: אם החברה ___ באגרסיביות רבה יותר, היא הייתה כובשת את השוק.
data.grammar_hint: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
data.common_mistake: Second conditional uses past simple; third conditional uses past perfect in the if-clause.

data.context_sentence: The manuscript is believed ___ by a team of anonymous scholars.
data.context_translation: מאמינים שהכתב יד ___ על ידי צוות של חוקרים אנונימיים.
data.grammar_hint: After "is believed", use passive infinitive. For completed past action: "to have been + past participle".
data.common_mistake: "To be written" suggests future or general; "to have been written" refers to a completed past action.

data.question_text: Choose the correct reduced relative clause:
data.context_sentence: The documents ___ at the archive contain evidence of the transaction.
data.context_translation: המסמכים ___ בארכיון מכילים ראיות לעסקה.
data.grammar_hint: Reduced relative clause: past participle replaces "which were + past participle". "Documents stored" = "documents which were stored".
data.common_mistake: "Storing" is active — documents do not store themselves. Use past participle "stored" for passive meaning.

data.context_sentence: Arrange the words to form a morning routine sentence.
data.context_translation: סדר את המילים ליצירת משפט על שגרת בוקר.
data.correct_answer: Every morning I drink a cup of coffee before work
data.common_mistake: Remember: subject (I) comes before the verb (drink) in declarative sentences.

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence about confirmed travel plans.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט על תוכניות נסיעה מאושרות.
data.correct_answer: We are planning to visit Japan next summer
data.common_mistake: "Planning to" expresses a firm, already-arranged intention — similar in meaning to "going to."

data.context_sentence: Build a passive-voice sentence about a rescheduled meeting.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט בגוף סביל על ישיבה שנדחתה.
data.correct_answer: The meeting has been rescheduled to Thursday afternoon
data.common_mistake: Present perfect passive: "has/have been + past participle." Note: "rescheduled TO" not "rescheduled FOR."

data.context_sentence: Build a first conditional sentence about finishing work on time.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט תנאי ראשון על סיום עבודה בזמן.
data.correct_answer: If you submit the report by noon we will review it today
data.common_mistake: First conditional: "If + present simple, will + base verb." No comma is needed when the main clause comes first.

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence about the effects of climate change.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט על השפעות שינויי האקלים.
data.correct_answer: Scientists warn that rising temperatures will affect ecosystems worldwide
data.common_mistake: Notice "affect" (verb) vs "effect" (noun). "Rising temperatures will affect ecosystems" — affect is the action verb here.

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence about the global impact of artificial intelligence.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט על ההשפעה הגלובלית של בינה מלאכותית.
data.correct_answer: Artificial intelligence is transforming the way businesses operate globally
data.common_mistake: "The way businesses operate" is a noun phrase, not a relative clause. No "that" or "which" is needed here.

data.context_sentence: Build a present perfect sentence about travel experience.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט בהווה מושלם על ניסיון טיול.
data.correct_answer: I have never been to South America but I hope to go someday
data.common_mistake: "Never" is placed between "have" and the past participle. "Have been to" means visited — "have gone to" means went and is still there.

data.context_sentence: Build a past simple narrative sentence.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט עבר פשוט נרטיבי.
data.correct_answer: She woke up early checked her phone and then made breakfast
data.common_mistake: Past simple with a sequence of actions: use commas for longer lists. "Woke up" is an irregular verb — not "waked up."

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence with a defining relative clause.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט עם פסוקית שם עצם מגדירה.
data.correct_answer: The colleague who helped me with the project received a promotion
data.common_mistake: Defining relative clauses have no commas — they identify which person/thing you mean.

data.context_sentence: Build a reported speech sentence.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט בדיבור עקיף.
data.correct_answer: The manager told the team that the deadline would be moved to Friday
data.common_mistake: "Will" changes to "would" in reported speech. "The deadline will be moved" → "the deadline would be moved."

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence giving strong advice.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט שנותן עצה חזקה.
data.correct_answer: You should drink at least eight glasses of water every day
data.common_mistake: "Should" for advice is followed by the base infinitive (not "to drink"). Example: "should drink" not "should to drink."

data.context_sentence: Build a superlative sentence about a city.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט עם תואר השוואה עליון על עיר.
data.correct_answer: Tokyo is one of the most densely populated cities in the world
data.common_mistake: "One of the most…" requires a plural noun (cities, not city). Always: "one of the most + plural noun."

data.context_sentence: Arrange the words to make a simple greeting.
data.context_translation: סדר את המילים ליצירת ברכה פשוטה.
data.common_mistake: In English, names are capitalised: "Anna" not "anna".

data.context_sentence: Build a simple sentence about what you like.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט פשוט על מה שאתה אוהב.

data.context_sentence: Build a formal passive sentence about a policy decision.

data.common_mistake: Passive voice: subject + was/were + past participle + by + agent.

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence with a relative clause about a researcher.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט עם משפט יחס על חוקר.

data.context_sentence: Build a complex reported-speech sentence.

data.context_sentence: Build a simple question about the time.

data.common_mistake: Question word order: What + auxiliary + subject — "What time is it?"

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence about a daily habit.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט על הרגל יומי.

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence about ordering food.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט על הזמנת אוכל.
data.correct_answer: I would like a salad and a glass of juice
data.common_mistake: Polite requests use "I would like" — not "I want" in formal settings.

data.context_sentence: Build a present continuous sentence about right now.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט בהווה מתמשך על מה שקורה עכשיו.
data.correct_answer: They are studying for the exam in the library
data.common_mistake: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing for actions happening now.

data.context_sentence: Build a past simple sentence about a trip.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט בעבר פשוט על טיול.
data.correct_answer: We visited three museums during our trip to Rome

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence about weekend plans.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט על תוכניות לסוף השבוע.
data.correct_answer: I am going to meet my friends at the beach on Saturday

data.context_sentence: Build a present perfect sentence about life experience.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט בהווה מושלם על ניסיון חיים.
data.correct_answer: She has lived in Tel Aviv for five years
data.common_mistake: Use "for" with a duration (five years) and "since" with a starting point.

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence giving permission.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט שנותן הרשאה.
data.correct_answer: You may use my laptop while I am in a meeting
data.common_mistake: "May" for permission is more formal than "can" — both are correct in casual speech.

data.context_sentence: Build a comparative sentence about two cities.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט השוואתי על שתי ערים.
data.correct_answer: Haifa is more relaxed than Tel Aviv in the evenings
data.common_mistake: Long adjectives use "more + adjective" — not "-er": "more relaxed" not "relaxeder".

data.context_sentence: Build a second conditional sentence.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט תנאי שני.
data.correct_answer: If I had more time I would learn another language
data.common_mistake: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb — for hypothetical situations.

data.context_sentence: Build a passive sentence about a completed task.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט פסיבי על משימה שהושלמה.
data.correct_answer: The report was finished by the team yesterday afternoon
data.common_mistake: Past passive: was/were + past participle. "Finished" not "finish".

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence with a relative clause about a book.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט עם פסוקית יחס על ספר.
data.correct_answer: The novel that won the prize has been translated into twenty languages
data.common_mistake: Use "that" or "which" for things. "Who" is for people only.

data.context_sentence: Build a reported speech sentence about a warning.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט בדיבור מדווח על אזהרה.
data.correct_answer: The doctor warned that smoking could damage his lungs
data.common_mistake: "Can" shifts to "could" in reported speech when the reporting verb is past.

data.context_sentence: Build a sentence about a successful negotiation.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט על משא ומתן מוצלח.
data.correct_answer: After lengthy negotiations both sides agreed on a fair compromise
data.common_mistake: "Agree on" a topic/decision. "Agree with" a person. "Agree to" a proposal.

data.context_sentence: Build a formal academic sentence about research findings.
data.context_translation: בנה משפט אקדמי רשמי על ממצאי מחקר.
data.correct_answer: The findings suggest that early intervention significantly improves long term outcomes
data.common_mistake: Academic writing often uses "suggest" (not "prove") to present cautious conclusions.

data.context_sentence: אני הולך לעבודה כל יום בשעה שמונה בבוקר.
data.context_translation: I go to work every day at eight in the morning.
data.correct_answer: I go to work every day at eight in the morning.
alternate_answers: I go to work every day at 8 in the morning.
Every day I go to work at eight in the morning.
I go to work at eight every morning.
data.common_mistake: Present Simple for routines. Do not use "I am going" — that is for actions happening right now.

data.context_sentence: אמש הלכנו למסעדה איטלקית וזמנו פסטה.
data.context_translation: Last night we went to an Italian restaurant and ordered pasta.
data.correct_answer: Last night we went to an Italian restaurant and ordered pasta.
alternate_answers: We went to an Italian restaurant last night and ordered pasta.
Last night, we went to an Italian restaurant and ordered pasta.
data.common_mistake: "Went" and "ordered" are both Past Simple irregular/regular verbs. Remember "go → went."

data.context_sentence: מעולם לא ביקרתי ביפן, אבל מאוד רוצה ללכת.
data.context_translation: I have never been to Japan, but I really want to go.
data.correct_answer: I have never been to Japan, but I really want to go.
alternate_answers: I've never been to Japan, but I really want to go.
I have never visited Japan, but I really want to go.
data.common_mistake: "Never been to" is Present Perfect for experience. Do not use "I never went to Japan" — that requires a time reference.

data.context_sentence: אם היה לי יותר זמן, הייתי לומד גיטרה.

data.correct_answer: If I had more time, I would learn to play the guitar.
alternate_answers: If I had more time, I would learn guitar.
I would learn to play the guitar if I had more time.
data.common_mistake: Second conditional: "If + past simple, would + base verb." This describes a hypothetical, not a real situation.

data.context_sentence: הדוח נכתב על ידי שלושה חוקרים ופורסם בחודש שעבר.
data.context_translation: The report was written by three researchers and published last month.
data.correct_answer: The report was written by three researchers and published last month.
alternate_answers: The report was written by three researchers and was published last month.
data.common_mistake: Passive voice: "was written by." In sequences, you can drop the second "was": "written and published."

data.context_sentence: אתה חייב לסיים את הפרויקט לפני הדדליין, אחרת הלקוח יבטל את ההזמנה.
data.context_translation: You must finish the project before the deadline, or the client will cancel the order.
